## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Collect signed/attributable owner decisions and merge contract drafts through one serialized steward, preserving prior decisions and explicit supersession links.
2. Record formal adoption of this finer-grained dispatch graph; explain the intentional early isolation work and which original M02 gates are expanded, not silently bypassed.
3. Create a conformance oracle mapping each invariant to legal, illegal, boundary, race and restart vectors, including status/action combinations.
4. Update contract/schema/protocol/workflow identities together without relabeling incompatible fixtures as compatible.
5. Link unresolved external legacy/platform inputs to their blocking future acceptance tasks while confirming no implementation depends on an unapproved semantic decision.
6. Validate all references, route names, schemas, task DAG and independent review assignments before releasing the contract candidate.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] No implementation task is dispatchable while one of its semantic decision prerequisites is unresolved.
- [ ] All 48 M02 obligations have explicit coverage and no historical gate is fabricated.
- [ ] The contract validator detects version drift and missing required scenarios rather than accepting a hand-edited success label.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

For pure-domain or documentation work, test the applicable deterministic/contract cases and record why process races do not apply; do not invent a runtime pass.

Never hand-seed a passing receipt, normalize an incompatible DTO in the harness, or reuse a fake controller as acceptance. Record command argv/cwd, exit code, tool/runtime versions, source/binary hash, raw response/readback and artifact digests. Do not fabricate a result when a required capability is unavailable.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. Non-code work must provide equivalent verifiable artifacts rather than a generic “done.”

On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. No destructive reset, live-lock breaking or rewriting historical evidence is a recovery shortcut.

The independent review/reconciliation/revalidation chain is [PF-S01-T90](#file-sprints-pf-s01-tasks-pf-s01-t90-md) → [PF-S01-T91](#file-sprints-pf-s01-tasks-pf-s01-t91-md) → [PF-S01-T92](#file-sprints-pf-s01-tasks-pf-s01-t92-md). 4. Model evaluated-at and next-change timestamps through an injected clock value.
5. Define typed integrity scope and permitted-action inputs independently of transport availability.
6. Publish pure test builders for valid and invalid canonical fact combinations without using them as service acceptance receipts.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] Malformed and contradictory inputs produce explicit diagnostics rather than accidentally valid defaults.
- [ ] The domain compiles without store/service/process/TUI imports.
- [ ] A field named revision cannot be substituted for a fence or unrelated revision type.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

## 7. Validation instructions and failure cases

Use [the validation playbook](#file-validation-validation-playbook-md) and the [real-service acceptance matrix](#file-validation-acceptance-matrix-md). Before implementation, capture the current failing/unsupported behavior; after changes run the positive cases, the explicit rejection cases above and the relevant stale-revision, wrong-project, wrong-principal, deadline and retry/readback boundaries. cargo test --locked -p boreal-domain


**Task-specific test targets (proposed; runnable only after this task creates/registers them):**

```sh
cargo test --locked -p boreal-domain --test production_decision_inputs
```

Unit/property inputs and owned corrupt-record setup are permitted when labeled accurately. Successful **service/lifecycle/release** evidence must use the actual built service, genuine declared verifier execution, valid attributable receipts and real required reviewer identities. Never hand-seed a passing receipt, normalize an incompatible DTO in the harness, or reuse a fake controller as acceptance. Record command argv/cwd, exit code, tool/runtime versions, source/binary hash, raw response/readback and artifact digests. Do not fabricate a result when a required capability is unavailable.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. Non-code work must provide equivalent verifiable artifacts rather than a generic “done.”

On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. - [ ] A cycle with deferred tasks reports reconciled scope without claiming those tasks succeeded.
- [ ] A container with normal queued work does not appear as a hard-blocked executable task.
- [ ] Corrupt descendants cannot create a misleading 100 percent accepted rollup.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. ## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Resolve the selected project from the working directory or explicit selector, with no fallback to a prior/global project.
2. Make initialization explicit and validate project ID, database instance and canonical workspace binding before exposing any data.
3. Reject absent, stale, foreign, malformed and mismatched metadata with typed run-init/rebind guidance.
4. Define move/restore/clone handling from the accepted contract: bind an existing identity only by an explicit authorized operation.
5. Prevent reading the database before selected-project identity is established; avoid foreign names in error/detail output.
6. Preserve existing setup UX where compatible and keep initialization idempotent without enrolling new privileged actors.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] Two temporary directories with overlapping IDs cannot read each other through implicit discovery.
- [ ] A copied metadata file cannot silently select another project database.
- [ ] Repeated initialization cannot become an actor-creation or role-escalation route.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. ## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Bind each session to an authenticated principal, harness identity, project, runtime identity and supported capability version.
2. Enforce one live execution per session while allowing an actor to have separately authorized sessions under explicit capacity rules.
3. Record delegation chain and effective permissions; prohibit delegated sessions from claiming independence from their original principal when policy forbids it.
4. Define session liveness separately from task progress and preserve ended/revoked session history.
5. Reject a different session silently adopting a live attempt; require the explicit recovery/adoption path.
6. Provide bounded actor/session context to action decisions without exposing secrets.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] Two sessions of one principal cannot bypass configured review independence.
- [ ] Revoked or foreign sessions cannot heartbeat, finish or review another project execution.
- [ ] Session restart/re-registration does not silently inherit a stale fence.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

Before implementation, capture the current failing/unsupported behavior; after changes run the positive cases, the explicit rejection cases above and the relevant stale-revision, wrong-project, wrong-principal, deadline and retry/readback boundaries. For pure-domain or documentation work, test the applicable deterministic/contract cases and record why process races do not apply; do not invent a runtime pass.

```sh
cargo test --locked -p boreal-application
cargo test --locked -p boreal-store
```


**Task-specific test targets (proposed; runnable only after this task creates/registers them):**

```sh
cargo test --locked -p boreal-application --test production_principal_sessions
```

Unit/property inputs and owned corrupt-record setup are permitted when labeled accurately. Successful **service/lifecycle/release** evidence must use the actual built service, genuine declared verifier execution, valid attributable receipts and real required reviewer identities. Never hand-seed a passing receipt, normalize an incompatible DTO in the harness, or reuse a fake controller as acceptance. Record command argv/cwd, exit code, tool/runtime versions, source/binary hash, raw response/readback and artifact digests. Do not fabricate a result when a required capability is unavailable.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. Non-code work must provide equivalent verifiable artifacts rather than a generic “done.”

On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. No destructive reset, live-lock breaking or rewriting historical evidence is a recovery shortcut.

## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Audit all source/blob/memory/receipt/operation lookup APIs for project filtering and authorization, including indirect references.
2. Reject foreign artifact IDs and paths even when they exist locally or have the same content hash.
3. Scope caches, index keys, diagnostic details, operation readback and pagination cursors by project/database/authority identity.
4. Prevent source text or cited documents from injecting trusted command directives or changing project selection.
5. Define explicit export/import/grant as the only future cross-project transfer mechanism; do not introduce a global canonical registry.
6. Test overlapping IDs and identical hashes in two projects through read and mutation APIs.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] Project A cannot query or use Project B evidence, memory, operation outcomes or diagnostics.
- [ ] Cached data is never considered authenticated merely because it was loaded earlier.
- [ ] A foreign source attachment cannot become proof or guidance for a local task without an explicit permitted import.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

## 7. Validation instructions and failure cases

Use [the validation playbook](#file-validation-validation-playbook-md) and the [real-service acceptance matrix](#file-validation-acceptance-matrix-md). Before implementation, capture the current failing/unsupported behavior; after changes run the positive cases, the explicit rejection cases above and the relevant stale-revision, wrong-project, wrong-principal, deadline and retry/readback boundaries. For pure-domain or documentation work, test the applicable deterministic/contract cases and record why process races do not apply; do not invent a runtime pass.

**Existing seed commands** (from the supplied repository, not a claim they currently pass):

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked -p boreal-application
```


**Task-specific test targets (proposed; runnable only after this task creates/registers them):**

```sh
cargo test --locked -p boreal-application --test production_cross_project_scope
```

Unit/property inputs and owned corrupt-record setup are permitted when labeled accurately. Successful **service/lifecycle/release** evidence must use the actual built service, genuine declared verifier execution, valid attributable receipts and real required reviewer identities. Never hand-seed a passing receipt, normalize an incompatible DTO in the harness, or reuse a fake controller as acceptance. Record command argv/cwd, exit code, tool/runtime versions, source/binary hash, raw response/readback and artifact digests. Do not fabricate a result when a required capability is unavailable.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. Non-code work must provide equivalent verifiable artifacts rather than a generic “done.”

On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. No destructive reset, live-lock breaking or rewriting historical evidence is a recovery shortcut.

The independent review/reconciliation/revalidation chain is [PF-S04-T90](#file-sprints-pf-s04-tasks-pf-s04-t90-md) → [PF-S04-T91](#file-sprints-pf-s04-tasks-pf-s04-t91-md) → [PF-S04-T92](#file-sprints-pf-s04-tasks-pf-s04-t92-md). This card remains an unaccepted plan until those required records exist.

# PF-S05 — Versioned service, durable operations and snapshot plumbing

**State at issue:** proposed / every task unaccepted.  
**Goal:** Expose the canonical Rust decision and transaction model through one authenticated, bounded service contract with replay/readback and consistent notifications.

## Entry, leaf joins and exit

**Hard entry gate tasks:** PF-S02-T92, PF-S03-T92, PF-S04-T92  
**Additional cross-sprint joins on named leaves:** None beyond sprint entry gates.  
**Independent review:** `PF-S05-T90` → **reconciliation:** `PF-S05-T91` → **exit revalidation:** `PF-S05-T92`.

All entry gates must be accepted before code work in this sprint. Individual leaf prerequisites may add later joins. In particular PF-S09 may begin its independent planning foundation after PF-S02/PF-S03/PF-S04, but PF-S09-T06 cannot begin until PF-S08-T92 is accepted. This is not early sprint acceptance.

## Required context

Read [the plan entry point](#file-readme-md), [dispatch rules](#file-execution-parallel-dispatch-md), [shared-file locks](#file-execution-shared-files-md), [the validation playbook](#file-validation-validation-playbook-md) and the selected leaf. Relevant baseline references: [R-PROTOCOL](#file-reference-context-r-protocol-md), [R-PROTOCOL-CODE](#file-reference-context-r-protocol-code-md), [R-ERRORS](#file-reference-context-r-errors-md), [R-SERVICE-HOST](#file-reference-context-r-service-host-md), [R-SERVICE-TRANSPORT](#file-reference-context-r-service-transport-md), [R-APP-OP](#file-reference-context-r-app-op-md), [R-APP-STATUS](#file-reference-context-r-app-status-md).

**Risk to preserve:** Transport success is not mutation success. Unknown operations, cursor gaps and cached actor context must not let clients invent outcomes or policy.

## Task-by-task execution map

| Task | Bounded outcome | Lane | Additional task prerequisites | Initial state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| [PF-S05-T02](#file-sprints-pf-s05-tasks-pf-s05-t02-md) | Implement one application command executor and transaction contract | APPLICATION | PF-S05-T01 | not_started |
| [PF-S05-T03](#file-sprints-pf-s05-tasks-pf-s05-t03-md) | Implement request admission, idempotency and definitive readback | SERVICE | PF-S05-T01, PF-S05-T02 | not_started |
| [PF-S05-T04](#file-sprints-pf-s05-tasks-pf-s05-t04-md) | Integrate production service host and single-writer queue | SERVICE | PF-S05-T01, PF-S05-T02, PF-S05-T03 | not_started |
| [PF-S05-T05](#file-sprints-pf-s05-tasks-pf-s05-t05-md) | Assemble canonical reads and server-owned action descriptors | APPLICATION | PF-S05-T01, PF-S05-T02 | not_started |
| [PF-S05-T06](#file-sprints-pf-s05-tasks-pf-s05-t06-md) | Implement revision-consistent pagination and subscription recovery | SERVICE | PF-S05-T01, PF-S05-T04, PF-S05-T05 | not_started |
| [PF-S05-T07](#file-sprints-pf-s05-tasks-pf-s05-t07-md) | Implement durable external-job scheduling and readback hooks | SERVICE | PF-S05-T02, PF-S05-T03, PF-S05-T04 | not_started |
| [PF-S05-T08](#file-sprints-pf-s05-tasks-pf-s05-t08-md) | Add genuine service harness and negative proof controls | VALIDATION | PF-S05-T01, PF-S05-T03, PF-S05-T04, PF-S05-T05, PF-S05-T06, PF-S05-T07 | not_started |

## Parallelism and integration

Dispatch one task per named agent, never this entire sprint as one assignment. Tasks with all prerequisites accepted may run together only when their actual worker write sets do not overlap. Shared root/schema/protocol/registry/release edits are serialized by the named steward; a function range in one file is not a separate write lock. Task cards list existing files versus proposed new outputs and exact integration requests. Use `python3 tools/plan.py graph-ready` and `python3 tools/plan.py conflicts TASK_A TASK_B` from this plan folder as read-only aids; neither grants authority or edits application state.

## Required sprint acceptance

- [ ] Every leaf has accepted evidence and a complete handoff at its actual integrated source revision.
- [ ] All schema/protocol/contract/root registrations are integrated; no disconnected scaffolding or test-only success path remains.
- [ ] Independent review records all findings (or explicit `no_findings`) with attributable reviewer identity.
- [ ] Reconciliation fixes every required issue or documents a justified noncritical disposition; mandatory safety/authority/proof/isolation work is nonwaivable.
- [ ] Exact-tree revalidation reruns the affected focused and required integration/native checks, preserving failures and unsupported results.
- [ ] Only `PF-S05-T92` acceptance unlocks ordinary successor sprint entry; publication and final production completion have additional explicit gates.

## Dispatch and evidence

The live coordinator ledger is execution/STATE.json (`execution/STATE.json` in the folder pack); the source/evidence handoff template is [TASK_HANDOFF.md](#file-templates-task-handoff-md). Use `project/validation/production/tasks/<TASK-ID>/attempt-<N>/` for task evidence and `project/validation/production/sprints/PF-S05/` for sprint findings/reconciliation/revalidation. These are proposed execution outputs, not evidence supplied with this plan.

## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

2. Bind replay to project/database epoch, principal, command, target and request digest.
3. Expose operation status for pending, committed, rejected and unresolved cases with safe retry/readback advice.

6. Avoid client-generated new IDs for automatic retry of the same uncertain mutation.

## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Schedule external work only from committed job intents with scoped identity and idempotency keys.

3. Record job ownership/heartbeat/result independently from task execution ownership.
4. Reconcile crash-after-side-effect through artifact/commit/process readback; do not rerun a non-idempotent effect blindly.
5. Bound job concurrency, output retention and cancellation acknowledgement.
6. Ensure recovery jobs cannot grant a new work fence or overwrite a committed accepted outcome by themselves.

## Parallelism and integration

Dispatch one task per named agent, never this entire sprint as one assignment. Tasks with all prerequisites accepted may run together only when their actual worker write sets do not overlap. Shared root/schema/protocol/registry/release edits are serialized by the named steward; a function range in one file is not a separate write lock. Task cards list existing files versus proposed new outputs and exact integration requests. Use `python3 tools/plan.py graph-ready` and `python3 tools/plan.py conflicts TASK_A TASK_B` from this plan folder as read-only aids; neither grants authority or edits application state.

## Required sprint acceptance

- [ ] Every leaf has accepted evidence and a complete handoff at its actual integrated source revision.
- [ ] All schema/protocol/contract/root registrations are integrated; no disconnected scaffolding or test-only success path remains.
- [ ] Independent review records all findings (or explicit `no_findings`) with attributable reviewer identity.
- [ ] Reconciliation fixes every required issue or documents a justified noncritical disposition; mandatory safety/authority/proof/isolation work is nonwaivable.
- [ ] Exact-tree revalidation reruns the affected focused and required integration/native checks, preserving failures and unsupported results.
- [ ] Only `PF-S06-T92` acceptance unlocks ordinary successor sprint entry; publication and final production completion have additional explicit gates.

## Dispatch and evidence

The live coordinator ledger is execution/STATE.json (`execution/STATE.json` in the folder pack); the source/evidence handoff template is [TASK_HANDOFF.md](#file-templates-task-handoff-md). Use `project/validation/production/tasks/<TASK-ID>/attempt-<N>/` for task evidence and `project/validation/production/sprints/PF-S06/` for sprint findings/reconciliation/revalidation. These are proposed execution outputs, not evidence supplied with this plan.

## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Select bounded ready candidates as hints and reread all authorization/requirements/dependency/recovery facts inside the final claim transaction.
2. Bind authenticated principal/session, entity revision, current accepted prerequisites, worktree/resource request and execution policy.
3. Create one attempt, reservation, fence, renewable lease and approved hard budget with operation/audit outcome atomically.
4. Return exact acceptance requirements, source/workspace constraints, deadlines and next permitted action.
5. Reject hold, pause, retry/schedule, wrong actor, missing requirement, unresolved recovery and conflicting execution/resource ownership.
6. Preserve deterministic ordering for automatic candidate selection without adding automatic harness launching.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] Competing claimers yield one accepted owner and typed losers with no duplicate reservation.
- [ ] A displayed blocked/queued/paused/expired task cannot be claimed through any lower-level supported route.
- [ ] No claim is authorized from a stale candidate query alone.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

## 7. Validation instructions and failure cases

Use [the validation playbook](#file-validation-validation-playbook-md) and the [real-service acceptance matrix](#file-validation-acceptance-matrix-md). Before implementation, capture the current failing/unsupported behavior; after changes run the positive cases, the explicit rejection cases above and the relevant stale-revision, wrong-project, wrong-principal, deadline and retry/readback boundaries. For pure-domain or documentation work, test the applicable deterministic/contract cases and record why process races do not apply; do not invent a runtime pass.

**Existing seed commands** (from the supplied repository, not a claim they currently pass):

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked -p boreal-application
cargo test --locked -p boreal-store
```


**Task-specific test targets (proposed; runnable only after this task creates/registers them):**

```sh
cargo test --locked -p boreal-application --test production_claims
```

Unit/property inputs and owned corrupt-record setup are permitted when labeled accurately. Successful **service/lifecycle/release** evidence must use the actual built service, genuine declared verifier execution, valid attributable receipts and real required reviewer identities. Never hand-seed a passing receipt, normalize an incompatible DTO in the harness, or reuse a fake controller as acceptance. Record command argv/cwd, exit code, tool/runtime versions, source/binary hash, raw response/readback and artifact digests. Do not fabricate a result when a required capability is unavailable.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. Non-code work must provide equivalent verifiable artifacts rather than a generic “done.”

On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. No destructive reset, live-lock breaking or rewriting historical evidence is a recovery shortcut.

The independent review/reconciliation/revalidation chain is [PF-S06-T90](#file-sprints-pf-s06-tasks-pf-s06-t90-md) → [PF-S06-T91](#file-sprints-pf-s06-tasks-pf-s06-t91-md) → [PF-S06-T92](#file-sprints-pf-s06-tasks-pf-s06-t92-md). This card remains an unaccepted plan until those required records exist.

## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Implement isolated worktree or approved explicit resource/write-set reservations with canonical project path checks.

4. Record process/host/session identity and stop-observation provenance sufficient for safe resource release.
5. Require reconciliation when a prior owner may still write; an expired database fence alone is insufficient.
6. Define clean/dirty worktree handoff and preservation of uncommitted user/agent changes without destructive resets.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] A replacement is denied while the previous process is unconfirmed or still writing.

## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Use separate real harness processes and the production service for claim/accept/start/heartbeat/release paths.
2. Race claim/hold, claim/dependency edits, heartbeat/expiry, finish/expiry and release/replacement with stable operation IDs.
3. Keep a worker writing in a disposable protected worktree after lease expiry and verify replacement is denied until the approved stop/disposition.
4. Restart the service and reorder old-fence messages; retain exact source, runtime and clock evidence.
5. Exercise manual adoption and authorized recovery controls with actual principal/session identities.
6. Run negative controls proving the harness detects duplicate current ownership and fabricated safe-stop acknowledgements.

- [ ] Changing artifact bytes or subject fields is detected.
- [ ] A failed/late receipt remains queryable without becoming valid current proof.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

## 7. Validation instructions and failure cases

Use [the validation playbook](#file-validation-validation-playbook-md) and the [real-service acceptance matrix](#file-validation-acceptance-matrix-md). Before implementation, capture the current failing/unsupported behavior; after changes run the positive cases, the explicit rejection cases above and the relevant stale-revision, wrong-project, wrong-principal, deadline and retry/readback boundaries. For pure-domain or documentation work, test the applicable deterministic/contract cases and record why process races do not apply; do not invent a runtime pass.

**Existing seed commands** (from the supplied repository, not a claim they currently pass):

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked -p boreal-application
cargo test --locked -p boreal-store
```


**Task-specific test targets (proposed; runnable only after this task creates/registers them):**

```sh
cargo test --locked -p boreal-application --test production_receipt_provenance
```

Unit/property inputs and owned corrupt-record setup are permitted when labeled accurately. Successful **service/lifecycle/release** evidence must use the actual built service, genuine declared verifier execution, valid attributable receipts and real required reviewer identities. Never hand-seed a passing receipt, normalize an incompatible DTO in the harness, or reuse a fake controller as acceptance. Record command argv/cwd, exit code, tool/runtime versions, source/binary hash, raw response/readback and artifact digests. Do not fabricate a result when a required capability is unavailable.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. Non-code work must provide equivalent verifiable artifacts rather than a generic “done.”

On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. No destructive reset, live-lock breaking or rewriting historical evidence is a recovery shortcut.

1. Open/inspect required reviews against one immutable submission/proof context and pinned review gate.

5. Reject self-review, unauthorized review and review against an obsolete or foreign subject.
6. Keep review creation and routing idempotent with explicit operation outcomes.

- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. ## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Implement create/read/edit/publish/archive planning operations for milestones and tasks with stable IDs and the accepted parent model.
2. Validate title/description, parent kind, project membership, required profile and execution mode before publication.
3. Apply expected entity/proof revisions and preserve planning change audit; do not write display status.
4. Separate archive visibility from successful/cancelled lifecycle so hiding a record never satisfies dependencies.
5. Use the approved impact policy for edits to open/active/terminal work rather than a generic unrestricted update.
6. Return typed planning gaps and safe corrective actions for malformed or incomplete plans.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] A fresh project can create two milestones and valid tasks without cross-project parent references.
- [ ] Archive does not make a task accepted or remove prerequisite truth.
- [ ] Invalid parent/profile/terminal edit is rejected with a durable outcome and no partial plan mutation.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

## 7. Validation instructions and failure cases

Use [the validation playbook](#file-validation-validation-playbook-md) and the [real-service acceptance matrix](#file-validation-acceptance-matrix-md). Before implementation, capture the current failing/unsupported behavior; after changes run the positive cases, the explicit rejection cases above and the relevant stale-revision, wrong-project, wrong-principal, deadline and retry/readback boundaries. For pure-domain or documentation work, test the applicable deterministic/contract cases and record why process races do not apply; do not invent a runtime pass.

**Existing seed commands** (from the supplied repository, not a claim they currently pass):

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked -p boreal-application
cargo test --locked -p boreal-store
```


**Task-specific test targets (proposed; runnable only after this task creates/registers them):**

```sh
cargo test --locked -p boreal-application --test production_hierarchy
```

Unit/property inputs and owned corrupt-record setup are permitted when labeled accurately. Successful **service/lifecycle/release** evidence must use the actual built service, genuine declared verifier execution, valid attributable receipts and real required reviewer identities. Never hand-seed a passing receipt, normalize an incompatible DTO in the harness, or reuse a fake controller as acceptance. Record command argv/cwd, exit code, tool/runtime versions, source/binary hash, raw response/readback and artifact digests. Do not fabricate a result when a required capability is unavailable.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. Non-code work must provide equivalent verifiable artifacts rather than a generic “done.”

On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. No destructive reset, live-lock breaking or rewriting historical evidence is a recovery shortcut.

The independent review/reconciliation/revalidation chain is [PF-S09-T90](#file-sprints-pf-s09-tasks-pf-s09-t90-md) → [PF-S09-T91](#file-sprints-pf-s09-tasks-pf-s09-t91-md) → [PF-S09-T92](#file-sprints-pf-s09-tasks-pf-s09-t92-md). ## 4. Exclusive changes and off-limits boundaries

| Planned changed/output path | Baseline availability | Edit owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/application/src/rollups.rs` | proposed_new file | task worker; exclusive lock required |
| `crates/application/tests/production_rollup_projection.rs` | proposed_new file | task worker; exclusive lock required |

**Shared integration changes requiring coordinator/steward ownership:**

- `crates/application/src/lib.rs`

The worker may implement only its non-shared listed files and its evidence directory. Submit precise integration patches for shared files; one steward applies them serially on the combined tree. An unregistered module or unintegrated patch is not accepted. A directory scope excludes protected shared manifests unless the coordinator explicitly grants that steward token. All unlisted production paths, other worktrees, live databases, legacy originals, secrets and prior evidence are read-only. See [shared-file locks](#file-execution-shared-files-md) for conflict rules.

**Evidence directory:** `project/validation/production/tasks/PF-S10-T03/attempt-<N>/`. Replace `<N>` with a new attempt number; never overwrite an earlier failed run.

## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Compute accepted work, reconciled commitment scope, active attempts, queue/hold/review/proof/expiry gaps and overdue totals from canonical records.
2. Avoid double counting tasks across historical assignments and preserve cycle-specific commitment history.
3. Provide child summaries and critical blockers with exact affected subject IDs and safe next actions.
4. Distinguish empty/planned/active/reconciled/closed container presentation from executable task statuses.
5. Surface incomplete/unsafe scope as diagnostics rather than a false percentage.
6. Bind container-close readiness to exact scope revision and accepted/disposed descendants.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] Carry-over leaves correct historical and current cycle totals without duplicating accepted work.
- [ ] A container with queued children is not labeled a non-executable hard blocker.
- [ ] Cancelled/deferred work never inflates successful-completion percentage.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

## 7. Validation instructions and failure cases

Use [the validation playbook](#file-validation-validation-playbook-md) and the [real-service acceptance matrix](#file-validation-acceptance-matrix-md). Before implementation, capture the current failing/unsupported behavior; after changes run the positive cases, the explicit rejection cases above and the relevant stale-revision, wrong-project, wrong-principal, deadline and retry/readback boundaries. For pure-domain or documentation work, test the applicable deterministic/contract cases and record why process races do not apply; do not invent a runtime pass.

**Existing seed commands** (from the supplied repository, not a claim they currently pass):

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked -p boreal-application
```


**Task-specific test targets (proposed; runnable only after this task creates/registers them):**

```sh
cargo test --locked -p boreal-application --test production_rollup_projection
```

Unit/property inputs and owned corrupt-record setup are permitted when labeled accurately. Successful **service/lifecycle/release** evidence must use the actual built service, genuine declared verifier execution, valid attributable receipts and real required reviewer identities. Never hand-seed a passing receipt, normalize an incompatible DTO in the harness, or reuse a fake controller as acceptance. Record command argv/cwd, exit code, tool/runtime versions, source/binary hash, raw response/readback and artifact digests. Do not fabricate a result when a required capability is unavailable.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. Non-code work must provide equivalent verifiable artifacts rather than a generic “done.”

On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. No destructive reset, live-lock breaking or rewriting historical evidence is a recovery shortcut.

The independent review/reconciliation/revalidation chain is [PF-S10-T90](#file-sprints-pf-s10-tasks-pf-s10-t90-md) → [PF-S10-T91](#file-sprints-pf-s10-tasks-pf-s10-t91-md) → [PF-S10-T92](#file-sprints-pf-s10-tasks-pf-s10-t92-md). This card remains an unaccepted plan until those required records exist.

## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Integrate row-level store diagnostics into work/cycle/milestone projections without duplicate selectable identities.

## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Use a dedicated safe Git workspace and deterministic manifest for the approved publication layout.
2. Persist a publication job/intent before external Git writes and run Git outside the canonical work transaction.
3. Record expected parent/content identity and actual resulting commit; reconcile commit-created-before-database-acknowledged failures by readback.
4. Handle concurrent human edits, merge conflicts and interrupted publication without destructive reset or fabricated success.
5. Make replay idempotent against the original publication identity and preserve failed jobs.
6. Expose published-at-named-revision authority separately from live database drafts.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] Crash after Git commit cannot create duplicate publication or lose its database linkage.
- [ ] A human edit is preserved or reported as conflict, never overwritten to force a green test.
- [ ] Only a verified actual Git revision is returned as published authority.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. ## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Assign fixed/no_change/deferred disposition to every independent-review finding with specific supporting evidence.
2. For fixes, dispatch a bounded remediation leaf/attempt to the original or designated owner with one exclusive write set and explicit prerequisites; this coordinator task is not permission to edit every implicated crate.
3. Add discovered remediation leaves to the task graph and make this reconciliation depend on their accepted handoffs before it can close; validate the extended graph for cycles and write conflicts.
4. Integrate patches through shared-file stewards, preserve failed receipts/reviews/tests and record the new combined source identity.
5. Reject any deferral of must-have correctness, isolation, authority, evidence or recovery; optional deferrals require explicit owner approval, follow-up and visible limits.
6. Record an explicit no_findings/no_change disposition when appropriate, plus the exact revalidation matrix required on the final combined tree.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] Every finding has a justified disposition and every required correction is integrated and task-accepted.
- [ ] No failed evidence/history is deleted or relabeled to make the sprint green.
- [ ] The coordinator provides exact source identity and rerun requirements; successor sprints remain gated.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

## 7. Validation instructions and failure cases

Use [the validation playbook](#file-validation-validation-playbook-md) and the [real-service acceptance matrix](#file-validation-acceptance-matrix-md). Before implementation, capture the current failing/unsupported behavior; after changes run the positive cases, the explicit rejection cases above and the relevant stale-revision, wrong-project, wrong-principal, deadline and retry/readback boundaries. For pure-domain or documentation work, test the applicable deterministic/contract cases and record why process races do not apply; do not invent a runtime pass.

**Existing seed commands** (from the supplied repository, not a claim they currently pass):

```sh

# This artifact/coordination task must still prove its named acceptance criteria.
```


Unit/property inputs and owned corrupt-record setup are permitted when labeled accurately. Successful **service/lifecycle/release** evidence must use the actual built service, genuine declared verifier execution, valid attributable receipts and real required reviewer identities. Never hand-seed a passing receipt, normalize an incompatible DTO in the harness, or reuse a fake controller as acceptance. Record command argv/cwd, exit code, tool/runtime versions, source/binary hash, raw response/readback and artifact digests. Do not fabricate a result when a required capability is unavailable.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. Non-code work must provide equivalent verifiable artifacts rather than a generic “done.”

On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. No destructive reset, live-lock breaking or rewriting historical evidence is a recovery shortcut.

The independent review/reconciliation/revalidation chain is [PF-S11-T90](#file-sprints-pf-s11-tasks-pf-s11-t90-md) → [PF-S11-T91](#file-sprints-pf-s11-tasks-pf-s11-t91-md) → [PF-S11-T92](#file-sprints-pf-s11-tasks-pf-s11-t92-md). This card remains an unaccepted plan until those required records exist.

# PF-S12 — Legacy parity, backup/restore and explicit maintenance recovery

**State at issue:** proposed / every task unaccepted.  
**Goal:** Migrate supported historical data without manufactured success, protect full project state with consistent backups, and expose explicit safe maintenance/repair workflows.

## Entry, leaf joins and exit

**Hard entry gate tasks:** PF-S08-T92, PF-S09-T92, PF-S11-T92  
**Additional cross-sprint joins on named leaves:** None beyond sprint entry gates.  
**Independent review:** `PF-S12-T90` → **reconciliation:** `PF-S12-T91` → **exit revalidation:** `PF-S12-T92`.

All entry gates must be accepted before code work in this sprint. Individual leaf prerequisites may add later joins. In particular PF-S09 may begin its independent planning foundation after PF-S02/PF-S03/PF-S04, but PF-S09-T06 cannot begin until PF-S08-T92 is accepted. This is not early sprint acceptance.

## Required context

Read [the plan entry point](#file-readme-md), [dispatch rules](#file-execution-parallel-dispatch-md), [shared-file locks](#file-execution-shared-files-md), [the validation playbook](#file-validation-validation-playbook-md) and the selected leaf. Relevant baseline references: [R-LEGACYMAP](#file-reference-context-r-legacymap-md), [R-MIGRATIONDOC](#file-reference-context-r-migrationdoc-md), [R-MIGRATION-CODE](#file-reference-context-r-migration-code-md), [R-MIGRATION-V3](#file-reference-context-r-migration-v3-md), [R-BACKUP-TEST](#file-reference-context-r-backup-test-md), [R-PERF](#file-reference-context-r-perf-md), [R-DECISIONS](#file-reference-context-r-decisions-md).

**Risk to preserve:** The supplied v2 mapping is not the missing raw v1 evidence. Full retained parity cannot pass without representative originals or an explicit owner-approved scope change.

## Parallelism and integration

Dispatch one task per named agent, never this entire sprint as one assignment. Tasks with all prerequisites accepted may run together only when their actual worker write sets do not overlap. Shared root/schema/protocol/registry/release edits are serialized by the named steward; a function range in one file is not a separate write lock. Task cards list existing files versus proposed new outputs and exact integration requests. Use `python3 tools/plan.py graph-ready` and `python3 tools/plan.py conflicts TASK_A TASK_B` from this plan folder as read-only aids; neither grants authority or edits application state.

## Required sprint acceptance

- [ ] Every leaf has accepted evidence and a complete handoff at its actual integrated source revision.
- [ ] All schema/protocol/contract/root registrations are integrated; no disconnected scaffolding or test-only success path remains.
- [ ] Independent review records all findings (or explicit `no_findings`) with attributable reviewer identity.
- [ ] Reconciliation fixes every required issue or documents a justified noncritical disposition; mandatory safety/authority/proof/isolation work is nonwaivable.
- [ ] Exact-tree revalidation reruns the affected focused and required integration/native checks, preserving failures and unsupported results.
- [ ] Only `PF-S12-T92` acceptance unlocks ordinary successor sprint entry; publication and final production completion have additional explicit gates.

## Dispatch and evidence

The live coordinator ledger is execution/STATE.json (`execution/STATE.json` in the folder pack); the source/evidence handoff template is [TASK_HANDOFF.md](#file-templates-task-handoff-md). These are proposed execution outputs, not evidence supplied with this plan.

## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Use one machine-envelope serializer and stable exit-code mapping across all commands and aliases.

3. Include project/database/snapshot/operation identities and typed gaps without serializing secrets or internal backtraces by default.
4. Make help/discovery reflect actual required flags, auth, consequences and compatible versions.
5. Provide operation-show/readback with enough authority and request identity to resolve unknown outcomes safely.
6. Sanitize untrusted terminal control sequences in human-readable output while preserving machine JSON escaping.

## Parallelism and integration

Dispatch one task per named agent, never this entire sprint as one assignment. Tasks with all prerequisites accepted may run together only when their actual worker write sets do not overlap. Shared root/schema/protocol/registry/release edits are serialized by the named steward; a function range in one file is not a separate write lock. Task cards list existing files versus proposed new outputs and exact integration requests. Use `python3 tools/plan.py graph-ready` and `python3 tools/plan.py conflicts TASK_A TASK_B` from this plan folder as read-only aids; neither grants authority or edits application state.

## Required sprint acceptance

- [ ] Every leaf has accepted evidence and a complete handoff at its actual integrated source revision.
- [ ] All schema/protocol/contract/root registrations are integrated; no disconnected scaffolding or test-only success path remains.
- [ ] Independent review records all findings (or explicit `no_findings`) with attributable reviewer identity.
- [ ] Reconciliation fixes every required issue or documents a justified noncritical disposition; mandatory safety/authority/proof/isolation work is nonwaivable.
- [ ] Exact-tree revalidation reruns the affected focused and required integration/native checks, preserving failures and unsupported results.
- [ ] Only `PF-S14-T92` acceptance unlocks ordinary successor sprint entry; publication and final production completion have additional explicit gates.

## Dispatch and evidence

The live coordinator ledger is execution/STATE.json (`execution/STATE.json` in the folder pack); the source/evidence handoff template is [TASK_HANDOFF.md](#file-templates-task-handoff-md). Use `project/validation/production/tasks/<TASK-ID>/attempt-<N>/` for task evidence and `project/validation/production/sprints/PF-S14/` for sprint findings/reconciliation/revalidation. These are proposed execution outputs, not evidence supplied with this plan.

# PF-S15 — Production terminal workspace and recovery UX

**State at issue:** proposed / every task unaccepted.  
**Goal:** Deliver a premium, responsive service-client TUI with clear planning/execution/review/recovery surfaces, server-owned actions and safe behavior in short editor terminals and outages.

## Entry, leaf joins and exit

**Hard entry gate tasks:** PF-S13-T92  
**Additional cross-sprint joins on named leaves:** None beyond sprint entry gates.  
**Independent review:** `PF-S15-T90` → **reconciliation:** `PF-S15-T91` → **exit revalidation:** `PF-S15-T92`.

All entry gates must be accepted before code work in this sprint. Individual leaf prerequisites may add later joins. In particular PF-S09 may begin its independent planning foundation after PF-S02/PF-S03/PF-S04, but PF-S09-T06 cannot begin until PF-S08-T92 is accepted. This is not early sprint acceptance.

## Required context

Read [the plan entry point](#file-readme-md), [dispatch rules](#file-execution-parallel-dispatch-md), [shared-file locks](#file-execution-shared-files-md), [the validation playbook](#file-validation-validation-playbook-md) and the selected leaf. Relevant baseline references: [R-TUI-CLIENT](#file-reference-context-r-tui-client-md), [R-TUI-CONTROLLER](#file-reference-context-r-tui-controller-md), [R-TUI-DASHBOARD](#file-reference-context-r-tui-dashboard-md), [R-TUI-LAYOUT](#file-reference-context-r-tui-layout-md), [R-TUI-TRANSPORT](#file-reference-context-r-tui-transport-md), [R-TUI-INPUT](#file-reference-context-r-tui-input-md), [R-TUI-SMOKE](#file-reference-context-r-tui-smoke-md).

**Risk to preserve:** Do not recreate lifecycle or action policy in TypeScript. Small terminals must reduce decoration before hiding data, selection, escape or consequential confirmation context.

3. Reject contradictory status/reason/action fields rather than silently repairing service truth.
4. Preserve additive compatibility only where the approved protocol allows it; otherwise show upgrade/incompatible guidance.
5. Keep diagnostic entries merged by stable identity without creating duplicate selectable work.
6. Expose server-provided recovery actions under holds rather than disabling every mutation from a blocked label.

- [ ] No TypeScript branch computes claim/finish/release permission from status or gate counts.
- [ ] A blocked task can show an authorized safe stop action returned by the service.


Never hand-seed a passing receipt, normalize an incompatible DTO in the harness, or reuse a fake controller as acceptance. Record command argv/cwd, exit code, tool/runtime versions, source/binary hash, raw response/readback and artifact digests. Do not fabricate a result when a required capability is unavailable.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. Non-code work must provide equivalent verifiable artifacts rather than a generic “done.”

On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. No destructive reset, live-lock breaking or rewriting historical evidence is a recovery shortcut.

## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Launch the compiled TUI in real PTYs against the actual Rust service, not fake dashboard/controller data.
2. Perform plan/claim/verify/review/finish/release/recovery and project switch actions with genuine evidence and registered identities.
3. Exercise all listed dimensions, live resize, UTF-8 paste, multiline input, cancellation and terminal restoration.
4. Interrupt service before/after commit and verify stale view, original operation readback and no unintended retries.
5. Inject scoped corruption through an owned negative-test setup and verify valid siblings/disabled action explanations.
6. Retain PTY transcripts/screenshots as observations with raw service requests/outcomes; presentation fixtures remain supplementary.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] A mounted TUI action completes the same canonical operation as CLI/service with correct audit/readback.
- [ ] No fixture-side DTO normalization is used to hide a real protocol mismatch.
- [ ] All supported geometry/outage/input cases preserve safety and usable recovery.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

For pure-domain or documentation work, test the applicable deterministic/contract cases and record why process races do not apply; do not invent a runtime pass.

```sh

```

Unit/property inputs and owned corrupt-record setup are permitted when labeled accurately. Successful **service/lifecycle/release** evidence must use the actual built service, genuine declared verifier execution, valid attributable receipts and real required reviewer identities. Never hand-seed a passing receipt, normalize an incompatible DTO in the harness, or reuse a fake controller as acceptance. Record command argv/cwd, exit code, tool/runtime versions, source/binary hash, raw response/readback and artifact digests. Do not fabricate a result when a required capability is unavailable.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. Non-code work must provide equivalent verifiable artifacts rather than a generic “done.”

On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. No destructive reset, live-lock breaking or rewriting historical evidence is a recovery shortcut.

**Sprint:** [PF-S15 — Production terminal workspace and recovery UX](#file-sprints-pf-s15-sprint-md)  
**Type / priority:** `reconciliation` / `must_have`  
**Owner:** Integration coordinator (`COORD`); assign one named worker.  
**Initial state:** `not_started` / unaccepted. Live coordinator state is in execution/STATE.json (`execution/STATE.json` in the folder pack).  
**Parent exit gate:** [PF-S15-T92](#file-sprints-pf-s15-tasks-pf-s15-t92-md). No task card is a completion receipt.

## 1. Dependency and decision gate

**Explicit task prerequisites:** [PF-S15-T90](#file-sprints-pf-s15-tasks-pf-s15-t90-md)

**Sprint entry prerequisites, also mandatory:** [PF-S13-T92](#file-sprints-pf-s13-tasks-pf-s13-t92-md)

**Decision context:** Consume the accepted contract; do not reopen settled product policy within this task.

**External inputs needed for acceptance:** No extra named external input beyond prerequisites, a capable executor and required reviewer.

Read each direct prerequisite’s accepted handoff and exact integrated source/evidence identity before editing. Graph readiness is not permission: the coordinator must also provide the input revision, exclusive write lease, available executor and review owner. Do not start a successor from a worker’s unreviewed claim or a failed/expired assignment.

## 2. Outcome and why this task exists

Deliver a premium, responsive service-client TUI with clear planning/execution/review/recovery surfaces, server-owned actions and safe behavior in short editor terminals and outages.

**Task outcome:** Reconcile sprint findings and integrate bounded corrections. The ordered work and named acceptance checks below define its boundary; do not replace them with a broader rewrite or a thin scaffold.

**Known context/risk:** Do not recreate lifecycle or action policy in TypeScript. Small terminals must reduce decoration before hiding data, selection, escape or consequential confirmation context.

**Inherited M02 coverage:** S04-T07  
**Known findings to inspect/reproduce:** No single inherited finding; execute the stated contract and report new findings.  
**Final acceptance rows:** Contributes to its sprint exit gate and linked acceptance matrix; not a stand-alone release claim.

See [the complete original-obligation crosswalk](#file-reference-m02-crosswalk-md) and [the source/finding register](#file-reference-findings-md). Inherited report claims are partial/unaccepted; existing implementations may be retained only after this task proves the accepted contract.

## 4. Exclusive changes and off-limits boundaries

| Planned changed/output path | Baseline availability | Edit owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project/validation/production/sprints/PF-S15/reconciliation.md` | proposed_new file | task worker; exclusive lock required |
| `project/validation/production/sprints/PF-S15/remediation-map.json` | proposed_new file | task worker; exclusive lock required |

**Shared integration changes requiring coordinator/steward ownership:**

No additional shared integration file is anticipated. Any new need requires a reviewed path-change request.

The worker may implement only its non-shared listed files and its evidence directory. Submit precise integration patches for shared files; one steward applies them serially on the combined tree. An unregistered module or unintegrated patch is not accepted. A directory scope excludes protected shared manifests unless the coordinator explicitly grants that steward token. All unlisted production paths, other worktrees, live databases, legacy originals, secrets and prior evidence are read-only. See [shared-file locks](#file-execution-shared-files-md) for conflict rules.

**Evidence directory:** `project/validation/production/tasks/PF-S15-T91/attempt-<N>/`. Replace `<N>` with a new attempt number; never overwrite an earlier failed run.

## 5. Ordered implementation / investigation instructions

1. Assign fixed/no_change/deferred disposition to every independent-review finding with specific supporting evidence.
2. For fixes, dispatch a bounded remediation leaf/attempt to the original or designated owner with one exclusive write set and explicit prerequisites; this coordinator task is not permission to edit every implicated crate.
3. Add discovered remediation leaves to the task graph and make this reconciliation depend on their accepted handoffs before it can close; validate the extended graph for cycles and write conflicts.
4. Integrate patches through shared-file stewards, preserve failed receipts/reviews/tests and record the new combined source identity.
5. Reject any deferral of must-have correctness, isolation, authority, evidence or recovery; optional deferrals require explicit owner approval, follow-up and visible limits.
6. Record an explicit no_findings/no_change disposition when appropriate, plus the exact revalidation matrix required on the final combined tree.

## 6. Required acceptance checklist

- [ ] Every finding has a justified disposition and every required correction is integrated and task-accepted.
- [ ] No failed evidence/history is deleted or relabeled to make the sprint green.
- [ ] The coordinator provides exact source identity and rerun requirements; successor sprints remain gated.
- [ ] The effective prerequisites, owner decisions, schema/protocol impacts and any baseline discrepancy are explicitly accounted for.
- [ ] Focused checks plus the required integration layer ran on the actual combined source/artifact identity; missing tools, skipped native checks and fixture-only success are not accepted results.
- [ ] All changes remain within the granted boundary; shared-file patches are integrated, and failed receipts/reviews/attempts/test results are preserved.
- [ ] The complete handoff and evidence exist and the coordinator records acceptance. Compilation alone does not close this task or its sprint.

## 7. Validation instructions and failure cases

Use [the validation playbook](#file-validation-validation-playbook-md) and the [real-service acceptance matrix](#file-validation-acceptance-matrix-md). Before implementation, capture the current failing/unsupported behavior; after changes run the positive cases, the explicit rejection cases above and the relevant stale-revision, wrong-project, wrong-principal, deadline and retry/readback boundaries. For pure-domain or documentation work, test the applicable deterministic/contract cases and record why process races do not apply; do not invent a runtime pass.

**Existing seed commands** (from the supplied repository, not a claim they currently pass):

```sh
# Select the applicable existing commands from VALIDATION_PLAYBOOK.md.
# This artifact/coordination task must still prove its named acceptance criteria.
```


Unit/property inputs and owned corrupt-record setup are permitted when labeled accurately. Successful **service/lifecycle/release** evidence must use the actual built service, genuine declared verifier execution, valid attributable receipts and real required reviewer identities. Never hand-seed a passing receipt, normalize an incompatible DTO in the harness, or reuse a fake controller as acceptance. Record command argv/cwd, exit code, tool/runtime versions, source/binary hash, raw response/readback and artifact digests. Do not fabricate a result when a required capability is unavailable.

## 8. Handoff, review and recovery

Use [the task handoff template](#file-templates-task-handoff-md) and [the evidence record template](#file-templates-evidence-record-md). Include exact changed files, base/final source, decisions/invariants, before/after behavior, all executed checks and failures, schema/protocol/migration/security impact, operation/receipt/review IDs where applicable, residual risks and the next safe task. Non-code work must provide equivalent verifiable artifacts rather than a generic “done.”

On a new blocker, stop the affected mutation/scope, retain work and evidence, and file [a finding](#file-templates-finding-md) plus [a bounded change request](#file-templates-change-request-md). On unknown command outcome, use original operation readback; on a worker timeout, the coordinator confirms process/worktree stop before reassignment. No destructive reset, live-lock breaking or rewriting historical evidence is a recovery shortcut.

The independent review/reconciliation/revalidation chain is [PF-S15-T90](#file-sprints-pf-s15-tasks-pf-s15-t90-md) → [PF-S15-T91](#file-sprints-pf-s15-tasks-pf-s15-t91-md) → [PF-S15-T92](#file-sprints-pf-s15-tasks-pf-s15-t92-md). This card remains an unaccepted plan until those required records exist.
